articles.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship 'catch'
articles.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship undertakes a landmark test attempting to catch the returning booster with mechanical arms, a revolutionary approach to rocket reusability. This breakthrough could transform space launch economics and enable more frequent access to orbit.

articles.title: Space telescope Euclid sets the new standard for cosmology
articles.description: On July 1, 2023, the European Space Agency (ESA) launched the Euclid space telescope into space. Its mission: to create the largest and most detailed map of the universe ever made.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid space telescope launches to create an unprecedented 3D map of the universe and unlock the secrets of dark matter and dark energy. This landmark mission represents a transformative step in understanding the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
articles.description: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover discovers complex organic carbon in ancient Martian rocks, confirming a key building block for life existed on Mars. This groundbreaking finding strengthens the case that Mars once harbored conditions suitable for life.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A breakthrough supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe emerged from its cosmic dark age and became illuminated with stars and galaxies. This landmark computational achievement deepens our understanding of cosmic history.

articles.title: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX
articles.description: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented double-catch mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket is set to attempt an unprecedented double-catch mission, marking a historic milestone in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have found evidence of an extremely rare particle decay occurring only once per 10 billion events after a 42-year search, representing a major breakthrough in particle physics. This discovery brings scientists closer to understanding fundamental physics at the subatomic scale.

articles.title: 900 millions de galaxies : Euclid ouvre un trésor cosmique qui pourrait bouleverser notre vision de l'Univers
articles.description: Après plus d'un an à scruter les profondeurs du cosmos, le télescope spatial Euclid vient de franchir une étape décisive. Les astrophysiciens du monde entier vont pouvoir explorer une quantité vertigineuse de nouvelles données en plus d'une mosaïque d'images …
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope has catalogued 900 million galaxies after more than a year of observation, opening a cosmic treasure that could fundamentally transform our understanding of the universe. This massive dataset promises revolutionary insights into dark matter and cosmic structure.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope reveals a diverse gallery of gravitational lenses that will be targets for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope.

articles.title: Euclid's First Data Release: A Stepping Stone to its 3D Map of the Sky
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first huge batch of data. It's all part of the telescope's mission to study dark energy and dark matter. The telescope is busy creating the largest ever 3D map of the Universe with its huge 600 megapixel camera, and new images give us some highlights.
articles.summary: ESA's Euclid Space Telescope releases its first major data batch, advancing toward creating a comprehensive 3D map of the universe.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu's Sample Delivers Another Surprise
articles.description: Researchers compared the samples from asteroid Bennu with the Murchison meteorite and measured the amino acid β-alanine in both. Using new techniques, they were able to measure not only their isotopic compositions, but isotopic differences between individual atoms in the same molecule. The results show that some of the same pre-cursors to life formed in different conditions and positions in the protoplanetary disk.
articles.summary: Samples from asteroid Bennu reveal the presence of amino acids, providing insights into the chemical building blocks of life in the early solar system.

articles.title: Asteroid Mining Will Crash the Platinum Market, But That’s Good News for Earth
articles.description: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. Humanity is slowly getting closer to that reality. But if you ask asteroid mining skeptics, they will usually ask one specific question - what happens to the prices of all those rare materials once someone actually brings them back? A pair of system dynamicists from MIT directly tackled that question with a new paper titled Will AstroForge Collapse the PGM Market?
articles.summary: Asteroid mining technology promises to extract valuable resources like platinum from space, delivering economic benefits to Earth while advancing space industry capabilities. This represents a major step toward utilizing space resources for human prosperity.

articles.title: Automated assembly in space is the future and NOM4D is showing the way
articles.description: If we want big things in space, we'll have to build and assemble them there. Rocket fairings are not large enough to accommodate the large things we want to have in space. Not only that, but the stubborn rocket equation refuses to bend itself to our desires.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NOM4D demonstrates automated assembly technology that enables construction of large structures in space, overcoming payload constraints of rockets. This innovation opens possibilities for building ambitious megastructures and infrastructure beyond Earth.

articles.title: Hubble offers cosmic sampler of targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA's Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope captures a stunning gallery of gravitational lenses that will help the Roman Space Telescope identify promising targets for future observation. This collaboration advances our ability to study dark matter and distant galaxies.

articles.title: Space dust particles point to ancient heavy-oxygen water reservoir in the Kuiper belt
articles.description: Way out past the asteroid belt, another belt encircles the planets in our solar system. The Kuiper belt, beyond Neptune, preserves icy bodies that escaped much of the processing experienced by objects closer to the sun. Unlike the rocky and metallic asteroid belt, Kuiper belt objects are composed mostly of frozen water, methane and ammonia, mixed with rock and dust.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of space dust particles reveals evidence of an ancient water reservoir in the Kuiper Belt, expanding our understanding of water distribution across the solar system. This discovery illuminates the origins of our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
articles.description: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago. Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history.
articles.summary: Research suggests dark energy may have reversed from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago, offering new insights into the universe's mysterious expansion. This discovery could reshape our understanding of cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: Scientists reveal that Earth's water may have originated in our planet's early atmosphere rather than from external sources like comets. This discovery transforms our understanding of how life-sustaining water came to exist on Earth.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe uncovers hidden patterns in the Sun's magnetic fields, revealing surprising order within apparent chaos. This discovery advances our understanding of solar dynamics and space weather.

articles.title: Powerful Vulcan Centaur rocket launching for 1st time in 9 months today: Watch it live
articles.description: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket will launch 40 Amazon internet satellites to orbit today (Nov. 13). You can watch the liftoff — Vulcan's first since February —live here at Space.com.
articles.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket launches 40 Amazon internet satellites to orbit in its first flight in 9 months.

articles.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight
articles.description: SpaceX has inked a familiar phrase on the Starship rocket that will fly a historic mission today (Nov. 13) — "Don't panic." And the company has invoked those words before.
articles.summary: SpaceX displays a classic cultural reference on its Starship rocket ahead of today's historic double-catch test flight.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.description: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a hidden black hole or neutron star companion feeding on an unstable massive star, solving a 15-year mystery of unusual supernova-like eruptions.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years
articles.description: On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P, then bounced twice and got lost. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On November 12, 2014, the European Philae probe made history by landing on Comet 67P, despite bouncing twice and spending nearly 2 years lost.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?
articles.description: "It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size."
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket launching to orbit on November 13 will be exceptionally bright and visible in the night sky.

articles.title: Astronomers Solve Mystery of Disappearing Exoplanet TOI-2535 b
articles.description: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that disappeared from observations after seven years of monitoring, according to a study published Monday in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. The planet, designated TOI-2535 b, is located about 1,000 light…
articles.summary: Astronomers have solved the mystery of exoplanet TOI-2535 b, which disappeared from observations after seven years of monitoring.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live and work on the Moon, offering a unique opportunity to work on another world.

articles.title: Une nouvelle mini-lune tourne autour de la Terre, et on a cru que c’était un morceau d’Apollo 13
articles.description: Le Minor Planet Center a confirmé le 29 octobre 2026 que la Terre héberge une nouvelle mini-lune, un caillou de 1 à 2 mètres baptisé 2026 QQ8. Des scientifiques l'ont même soupçonné d'être un débris spatial, allant jusqu'à parler d'un reste de la mission Apol…
articles.summary: Earth has acquired a new mini-moon measuring 1-2 meters, confirmed by the Minor Planet Center, initially thought to be debris from Apollo 13. This discovery expands our understanding of Earth's transient natural satellites.

articles.title: Zum ersten Mal in der Geschichte baut Roboter eigenständig eine Struktur im Weltraum zusammen
articles.description: Ohne Menschen vor Ort hat ein Roboter im All autonom ein Bauteil errichtet. Es könnte der Anfang roboterbasierten Baus im Orbit sein.
articles.summary: A robot has autonomously assembled a structure in space for the first time without human presence, marking a historic milestone in space construction. This achievement could pave the way for robotic-based construction and assembly in orbit.

articles.title: NASA takes an all-hands-on-deck approach in its return to the Moon
articles.description: Senior NASA officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power gene…
articles.summary: NASA launches a comprehensive initiative to return humans to the Moon, announcing lunar contract awards and new partnerships. This all-hands-on-deck approach represents a major commitment to lunar exploration and establishing a sustainable human presence.

articles.title: 378 dias sem janelas: NASA termina mais uma experiência para preparar viagens a Marte
articles.description: A NASA concluiu recentemente a segunda missão CHAPEA, onde quatro voluntários passaram 378 dias num habitat simulado de Marte, construído por impressão 3D e sem janelas. O objetivo é preparar a futura exploração humana do planeta vermelho. Um ano de isolament…
articles.summary: NASA successfully completed the second CHAPEA mission where four volunteers spent 378 days in a simulated Martian habitat, advancing preparations for crewed Mars missions. This extended isolation study provides critical data for human long-duration spaceflight.

articles.title: Für Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel: Roboter baut autonom Strukturen im All
articles.description: Im Rahmen des von der US-Forschungsagentur Darpa finanzierten Nom4d-Projekts hat ein Caltech-Roboter erstmals autonom eine Struktur im All errichtet. Das soll künftig den Bau großer Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel erleichtern.weiterlesen auf t3n.de
articles.summary: A Caltech robot funded by DARPA has successfully built autonomous structures in space for solar panels and telescope mirrors, demonstrating robotic construction capabilities. This breakthrough opens possibilities for future orbital infrastructure development.
